problem: Modular object-goal navigation policies (exploration + last-mile/local policy) optimize each module independently, with no interplay in loss objectives, so the exploration module carries the full sparse-reward learning burden.
motivation: The final steps once the goal is visible are nearly deterministic and are well handled by geometric visuo-motor servoing. If the exploration module knew this exploitation ability existed, it could learn better, more goal-conditioned exploration with a shorter RL horizon and denser success signal.
key_idea: Let a geometric exploitation module take over once the goal is visible and close, and teacher-force it into the PPO rollouts so the neural exploration module is optimized knowing that exploitation will finish the job.
insight: Both decomposition and guidance help: the ablation goes 70.4 -> 71.5 (decomposition) -> 72.9 SR (plus guidance), with larger SPL gains. Guidance shortens the RL horizon, so exploration becomes more goal-conditioned: coverage drops from 63.5% to 59.8% while SCov rises 36.3 -> 39.1. With GT semantics SR is only 73.5, so the semantic segmentation accounts for a small part of the remaining errors. Most simulated failures (45%) are missing annotations, and the real-world gain depends on adapting embodiment and using a robust detector (Detic).
method: Exploration module: PIRLNav-style ResNet50 + 2-layer GRU policy with categorical actions, warm-started by IL on Habitat-Web human demos and fine-tuned with RL/PPO.

Phase transition: switch to exploitation when the semantic segmentation (RedNet in sim, Detic in real) contains the goal category and depth-inferred distance is <= delta (2.5 m); it switches back to exploration if the agent leaves these states (backtracking).

Exploitation module: lifts the goal mask to 3D with depth and intrinsics, takes the min-depth pixel as waypoint, plans with fast marching on a local depth map, recomputes the waypoint every step, and calls stop.

Guidance via teacher-forced PPO: rollout actions in the buffer come from the exploitation policy in exploit states and from the exploration policy otherwise, and value/advantage estimates use this behavior policy, shortening the horizon.
Efficiency metric SCov: success-weighted ratio of oracle shortest-path coverage to max(actual, oracle coverage), balancing success with exploration efficiency.
Real-robot transfer: retrain PIRLNav/XGX with robot height and camera parameters (600M PPO frames), use Detic for segmentation, Hector SLAM from 2D LiDAR for pose, and MPC for low-level actuation.

setting.backbone: ResNet50 + GRU exploration policy (PIRLNav init, IL then RL fine-tuned) + geometric exploitation module + RedNet/Detic segmentation
setting.training_data: IL warm-start on ~80k Habitat-Web human demonstrations, then PPO fine-tuning in HM3D train scenes (64 GPUs x 8 envs); RedNet trained on HM3D train; Detic off-the-shelf
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move forward, turn left/right, look up/down, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes) plus MiniGrid diagnostic and a real wheeled robot
setting.privileged: none (a GT-semantics variant is reported only as an upper bound)

numbers.backbone: same as XGX with GT semantics
numbers.evidence: Table 2 row 4: XGX + GT Semantics (upper bound) 73.5 / 39.8

numbers.method: Init. IL + fine-tune + Policy Decomposition (no guidance)

numbers.eval_set_note: 14 trajectories per method, 5 goal categories, 3 scenes (Apartment, Office, Food Court)
numbers.backbone: ResNet50+GRU adapted to robot embodiment + geometric exploit + Detic

numbers_note: Split 'val' used as the paper evaluates on the 2000-episode HM3D-val split. Exploration efficiency (SCov 39.1, Cov 59.8) is in Table 3 and not in the metrics above.
results: XGX reaches 72.9 SR / 35.7 SPL on HM3D ObjectNav val, beating the authors' PIRLNav reimplementation (70.4 / 34.1) and OVRL-V2 (64.7 / 28.1). On a real robot it gets 35.7 SR / 23.3 SPL versus 14.2 / 8.4 for adapted PIRLNav.
limitations: Most failures are missing annotations (45%), then exploration loops (18%) and missed staircases (16%); the exploration module is still under-exploring.
Depends on a segmentation model and a hand-tuned switching threshold; min-depth waypoint selection caused most real-robot failures.
Real-world evaluation is small (14 trajectories per method) and requires embodiment retraining; the simulation gain over PIRLNav is modest (+2.5 SR).
